title: A Will for the Portrait
premise: Retired detective Ivo Zhou, now barely keeping their failing bookshop afloat, receives a letter confessing to the murder of wealthy portraitist Edmund Vail — postmarked the day after Vail's funeral. The confession describes details never released to the public, and it names Ivo as the only person who can 'see what the family cannot.' As Ivo reenters the investigation unofficially, they discover the killer is someone inside Vail's household who has been feeding on the case file itself, manipulating both police and heirs. In the end Ivo unmasks the killer — Vail's devoted archivist, who murdered him to protect her own stolen identity as the true heir's daughter — and must choose between turning her in and honoring the love that drove her, ultimately choosing duty while quietly preserving one truth: the portrait Vail painted of her real father.
about_author: Isandro Thornbury is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent two decades transcribing confessions before turning to fiction. They write mysteries from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Cornish coast.

chapters.title: Postmarked Grief
chapters.summary: Ivo Zhou, dusting unsold stock in their failing bookshop, opens an anonymous confession to murder postmarked the day after Edmund Vail's funeral. The letter cites details only the killer could know. Ivo's POV; the beat is reluctant awakening — old instincts stirring against a life they tried to bury.

chapters.title: The House That Painted Him
chapters.summary: Ivo attends the wake at Vail's estate under a bookseller's pretext, cataloguing the grieving family: the brittle widow, the estranged son, and the quiet archivist Mara Voss. Third-person limited on Ivo. Emotional beat: unease beneath civility, as every mourner seems to be performing grief rather than feeling it.

chapters.title: What the File Never Said
chapters.summary: Ivo pulls favors from a former colleague and reads the official case file, discovering the confession letter contains facts absent from it — meaning the writer knows something the investigators missed, or fabricated it. Ivo's POV. Beat: cold dread; the killer isn't reacting to the case, they're authoring it.

chapters.title: A Second Letter
chapters.summary: Another letter arrives, addressed directly to Ivo, praising their 'sharp eye' and warning them off the widow. Ivo realizes they are being steered. Ivo's POV with a brief interlude from Detective Reyes chafing at jurisdiction. Beat: paranoia — hunter becoming quarry.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Drawer
chapters.summary: Snooping Vail's study, Ivo finds gaps in the correspondence archive and a decades-old photograph of a child no family member claims. Mara catches them there, calm and helpful, offering a key detail about Vail's final weeks. Alternating Ivo/Mara POVs. Beat: magnetic suspicion — charm that reads too perfectly.

chapters.title: Love Against the Ledger
chapters.summary: Ivo traces the photograph to a servant's daughter presumed dead thirty years ago, and uncovers Vail's secret payments to her mother — and a romance Vail hid even from his wife. Ivo's POV. Beat: tenderness entangled with motive; Ivo begins to understand a crime committed for love, not greed.

chapters.title: The Widow's Confession
chapters.summary: Cornered by Ivo's questions, the widow admits she knew of the affair and had hired someone to frighten Vail — but insists he was alive when she left. Her alibi checks out. Ivo's POV. Beat: despair; every suspect cleared except the one whose name Ivo keeps refusing to say.

chapters.title: Portrait of a Thief
chapters.summary: Ivo matches the archivist's handwriting to the letters and discovers 'Mara Voss' is the servant's daughter, living under a stolen identity inside the house that erased her. She has been reading the case file through Reyes's own clerk. Dual POV converging. Beat: heartbreak hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Last Sitting
chapters.summary: Ivo sets a trap: announcing publicly that the true heir's identity will be revealed, forcing Mara to come to the bookshop at night. She arrives not with a weapon but with the finished portrait of her father, and confesses everything — Vail died denying her, and she let him. Climax; alternating POVs. Beat: devastating intimacy between hunter and killer.

chapters.title: A Will for the Portrait
chapters.summary: Ivo turns Mara in but testifies to the full truth of her erasure, ensuring the court hears what the family buried. The bookshop gains unexpected customers drawn by the case; the portrait hangs above the till. Epilogue, Ivo's POV. Beat: bittersweet resolution — duty honored, love grieved, identity finally witnessed.
